newsitem.title: UK: New BSkyB boss "quite a little wizard" - Chisholm.
newsitem.headline: New BSkyB boss "quite a little wizard" - Chisholm.

text.p: BSkyB chief executive Sam Chisholm, stepping down at the end of the year, said his successor, Mark Booth, was the ideal man for the job.
"He is absolutely the right man to take this company forward," Chisholm told a news conference also attended by Booth, currently chief operating officer at JSkyB, News Corp's Japanese TV venture.
Chisholm described Booth as a "very experienced pay TV operator" and "quite a little wizard at what he does".
Chisholm said his asthma problems made it impossible for him to lead BSkyB through the three year cycle it was entering as it launched new digital services.
"If you set out to climb a mountain there is no point saying you don't feel well when you're halfway up."
Chisholm and his deputy David Chance, who has also had health problems, will both step down at the end of the year but remain as consultants and board members.
"We are embarking on a brand new era and we need a new management team to see it through," Chisholm added.
A successor to Chance has not yet been named but Chance himself said his consultancy agreement would see him working "pretty much" full time for the company until at least the middle of 1998.
Chisholm, who has made BSkyB one of the UK's corporate success stories of the 1990s, said that British broadcasting was "all the better" for the development of the pay TV giant.
